_about: WHERE A PICTURE IS DRAWN BETWEEN TICKS: the original's, which is the tick's own place.
Planning step 150 of docs/planning/2026-09-11-magic-portals-remaster.md (program wave 3a, PIC; the backlog's PORT-WIDE row 'the
picture of any body is drawn one tick behind the sim', found verifying step 78).
THE DECODE. The original draws every entity where its frame left it. A script's SetPositionXY is a b2Body::SetTransform inside the
frame's Update (ETHScene::Update, ETHScene.cpp:459-493: the physics step, then the always-active entities' callbacks, then the
scene's loop function, then the static callbacks), and the drawing that follows reads GetPosition() at draw time
(ETHRenderEntity.cpp:106 and :152, where ETHEntitySpriteRenderer holds the entity's pointer and not a position: ETHEntityRendering
Manager.cpp:45-75, ETHEntitySpriteRenderer.cpp:25-39; D10_check section 4a, DECODED from the C++). There is no interpolation in the
original: a body that moved in a frame is drawn moved in that same frame, the camera is read the same way (GetCameraPos at draw
time), and a particle system or a light an entity carries is placed from the same point that frame.
THE PORT BEFORE THIS STEP. buildSprites gave every body-linked quad (and the sky, the carried keys and diamonds, the knight, the
minions, the ghost: every picture the tick moves) an InterpolatedTransformComponent, and the camera an InterpolatedCamera
Component, and the engine's InterpolationSystem::Apply draws previousPosition -> currentPosition at the frame's alpha
(engine/src/core/InterpolationSystem.cpp:140-149). alpha is 0 on every --fixed-step frame (a frame is a tick and the accumulator is
spent), so the picture showed where the body stood a tick ago, 16.7 ms late, while everything the layer places from the sim's own

point (the lights, the halos, the emitters, every effect an owner carries, the tutorial hands, the shot and its marks) stood a tick ahead of it. The HUD and the pads are the screen's own overlay and were never behind anything.
Step 78 MEASURED it: the player's drawn left edge equalled its box exactly one frame late.
THE PORT NOW. MagicPortalsLayer::OnFixedUpdate ends by publishing the tick's end as BOTH ends of the interpolation for every
interpolated picture and for the camera (drawPicturesAtTick), so InterpolationSystem::Apply returns the tick's own place at any
alpha. The engine is not touched. Nothing the simulation reads changes: BeginTick still puts the authoritative transform back at
every tick's start, and a tap is mapped through the camera the last tick left - now the very camera the last frame drew.
REAL TIME. The default is the original's, in captures and at the 60 Hz the port is matched at (clock.json matched_hz): the
tick's own place. A display that outruns the tick would show each tick's picture for two or three frames - motion at 60 Hz steps
on a 120 or 144 Hz screen, where the original's own frames come at the display's rate - so there the engine's interpolation is
KEPT, for smoothness (the picture then stands up to one tick behind what the lights and effects read from the sim: under
17 ms at 60 Hz ticks, and not seen). THE SWITCH is smoothing.above_hz: while the mean rate of the frames the layer is handed
(OnUpdate's deltaTime, an exponential mean over window_frames, a stall longer than hitch_ticks ticks left out) is over it, the
layer publishes nothing and the engine interpolates as it did before this step; under release_below_hz it publishes again. 0 never
interpolates: the original's own at every rate. It is OFF in a --fixed-step run whatever its value (main.cpp tells the layer: a
run whose frames are the tick's own measures nothing and must reproduce), and a run of the 60 Hz the port is matched at is never
above it, so a capture and real time at 60 Hz both draw the tick's place.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: no gameplay (a picture only: no tick, route, sim state or tap mapping moves), the engine, the physics,
the script clock or any number another file carries.

_source: The PORT'S OWN, not the original's (it has no interpolation to decode): when to keep the engine's smoothing is a choice, marked
_guess. 80 Hz is a line between the 60 Hz the port is matched at and the 90, 120 and 144 Hz displays it would otherwise step on,
with 75 Hz screens left on the original's behaviour (one frame in five repeats a picture); 72 is the floor of a 10 % band, so a
display on the line does not flip; a 30-frame mean is half a second at 60 Hz and about a tenth of a second to cross the line
from the matched 60 Hz seed on a 144 Hz screen; a frame longer than two ticks is a load or a window drag and says nothing of
the display. Retune here: above_hz 0 turns smoothing off for good.
